PullRequest.Title: Remove legacy compilation from standalone web packaging
PullRequest.Body:
Standalone web packaging already uses esbuild, but its local tasks still run the old all-source compile/mangle pipeline first. This removes that redundant prerequisite while keeping its necessary setup explicit.

- Generate API proposal names and the shared build date before the existing web packaging chain.
- Reuse the shared esbuild wrapper with the `web` target instead of duplicating the subprocess implementation.
- Preserve codicons, web-extension/media preparation, NLS, minification/private-field conversion, and existing CDN source-map arguments.
- Leave legacy registrations, dependency manifests, server packaging, and NLS/CDN behavior unchanged.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Adding the esbuild standalone-web bundle behind a task that still required `compileBuildWithManglingTask` caused two independent whole-source build pipelines to run serially for each local web package; the first pipeline's emitted JavaScript was not consumed by the source-based esbuild bundle.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Local `gulp vscode-web` and `gulp vscode-web-min` packaging paid an unnecessary full-source compile, NLS generation, mangling, and filesystem emission before the actual esbuild bundle, increasing end-to-end build latency and CPU/I/O.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The local standalone-web packaging tasks now generate API proposal names and the shared build date, then proceed directly to the existing web-extension preparation and esbuild bundle. This removes one full repository-wide TypeScript/NLS/mangling pass and its `out-build` writes from every local web package while preserving bundle ordering and metadata.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Before the PR, the local `vscode-web`/`vscode-web-min` task series ran `compileBuildWithManglingTask` and then `vscodeWebTaskCI`, whose bundle step launched the standalone-web esbuild task. `compileBuildWithManglingTask` recursively reads `src/**`, runs the full build/NLS TypeScript pipeline and mangler, and writes `out-build`; `build/next/index.ts:523-570` shows the subsequent esbuild bundle independently bundles entry points directly from TypeScript source and cleans/writes its own output. The esbuild task's introduction at base line 174 therefore made the retained legacy compile redundant except for API-proposal generation and the date file. The changed task series removes that full compile while preserving those two setup operations explicitly.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local standalone-web packaging via `gulp vscode-web` or `gulp vscode-web-min`
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The task runs API-proposal generation, writes the shared date, copies codicons, packages web extensions/media, launches the standalone-web esbuild child process, removes the destination, and streams package contents to disk; all stages are serial and must complete before the package is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runs `git log -1 --format=%cI HEAD` to produce the deterministic build date.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess per local packaging invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same git subprocess ran once inside `compileBuildWithManglingTask` before the esbuild bundle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before extension preparation and bundling, but replaces the identical date generation formerly nested in the removed compile prerequisite.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawns Node to execute `build/next/index.ts bundle` for the `web` target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child process per packaging invocation; entry-point builds inside it remain concurrently scheduled exactly as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The file-local wrapper spawned the same Node command with the same web target and flags.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the main bundle stage and blocks packaging until all bundles, resources, standalone files, and asset post-processing complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Scans/packages built-in extensions and dependencies, cleans output directories, and streams the bundle and package contents to the destination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pass over the selected web extensions, dependency trees, and produced bundle per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same extension and package filesystem stages ran after an additional full `src/**` legacy compilation and emission.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These serial stages must complete before packaging returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with repository source size, the web bundle dependency graph, bundled extension count, and production dependency files. The removed legacy pass previously added a second repository-wide source traversal, TypeScript/NLS transformation, mangling pass, and `out-build` emission before the source-based esbuild bundle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Top-level stages use `task.series`; extension substeps are also serial. The esbuild child bundles entry points concurrently internally with `Promise.all`, unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both the old compile path and the esbuild path clean/rewrite outputs, so there is no persistent build-result cache to collapse the duplicate work; only OS filesystem caches may be warm. The PR preserves deterministic date reuse and extension grouping.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: task ordering, the full-source compile implementation, and esbuild's independent source-based bundle path are explicit in the repository.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact wall-clock savings depend on machine CPU, filesystem cache warmth, and repository state, but the eliminated full-source compile/mangle/write pass is directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression introduced. This scenario fixes a repeated-work regression by removing the redundant legacy whole-source build while retaining the API-proposal and date prerequisites; the fix was recorded for regression learning.

Scenarios.Scenario: Web product CI packaging via `core-ci` followed by `gulp vscode-web-min-ci`
Scenarios.CriticalPath: `core-ci` prepares shared outputs and date metadata, then the web CI task copies codicons, packages web extensions/media, launches one minified web esbuild bundle, removes the destination, and writes the package before archive creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawns Node for one minified, NLS-enabled standalone-web esbuild bundle with CDN source-map arguments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One web bundle child process for the CI package after `core-ci`; no extra child process is added by the shared-wrapper refactor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed local wrapper spawned the same command once with the same output, minification, NLS, target, and source-map URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks package streaming and archive creation until the web bundle completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rebuilds web extension assets, cleans the destination, and copies filtered bundle/dependency resources into the product directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped packaging pass over the selected extensions, dependencies, and bundle outputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operations occurred in the same order.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The bundle scales with web entry-point graphs; packaging scales with web extensions and dependency files. Effective boundary cardinality remains one esbuild process and one grouped packaging pipeline, not per source file or extension.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The web task stages are serial; the esbuild child retains its existing per-entry-point concurrent bundling. `core-ci` bundles desktop/server targets in parallel before this separate task, unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CI uses fresh/clean output directories; shared `out-build/date` from `core-ci` is reused by the web bundle. This diff does not change cache keys, negative caching, or coalescing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the pipeline invokes `core-ci` then the `-ci` task directly, and the old/new wrappers construct equivalent subprocess arguments.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CI duration varies with hosted-agent resources, but the diff preserves its process and filesystem operation counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance change: the shared helper refactor preserves CI boundary count, scheduling, target selection, and package cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Existing desktop, server, and server-web callers of the shared esbuild wrapper
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each existing caller still launches its configured bundle child process as part of its existing build task; the widened target type does not alter runtime control flow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawns the existing Node esbuild bundle command for desktop/server/server-web targets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one process per existing wrapper invocation, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical spawn implementation, arguments, and waiting semantics; only the accepted TypeScript target union is widened.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on each existing build task's bundle critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing bundle cost continues to scale with each target's entry-point graph; no new target invocation is introduced for these callers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing task-level and internal esbuild concurrency is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Output cleaning and build-date reuse remain unchanged for these targets.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the implementation body is unchanged and all existing call sites already pass explicit non-web targets.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the reviewed mechanism; this is a type-level extension only for existing callers.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. The PR removes a serial, repository-wide legacy compile/mangle/emission that had become redundant before local standalone-web esbuild packaging; that concrete regression fix was recorded. The shared wrapper preserves subprocess arguments and all changed scenarios preserve boundary cardinality, concurrency, cache behavior, and package ordering. No diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold.
